findings.current: “They’re made of ebony imported from the Southern Man.[^1] Wood harder than steel.”
findings.defect: The plural pronoun changes the subject from the single broken chair to multiple chairs, and the second sentence is an unnatural fragment.
findings.rationale: The Korean uses a singular implied subject referring to the chair and identifies ebony as a wood harder than steel.
findings.replacement: “It’s made of ebony imported from Nanman.[^1] The wood is harder than steel.”
findings.source: “남만에서 들여온 흑단목(黑檀木)일세. 쇠보다 단단한 목재지.”

findings.current: waiting for me with his eyes bulging.
findings.defect: The draft turns an angry glare into physically bulging eyes.
findings.rationale: 눈알을 부라리다 means to glare or stare fiercely in anger, not merely to have bulging eyes.
findings.replacement: waiting for me with a fierce glare.
findings.source: 전각을 나오자 젊은 호위, 아니 남궁세가의 소가주인 검룡 남궁옥이 눈알을 부라린 채 나를 기다리고 있었다.

findings.defect: The nonsensical “Yo—” loses Taekyung beginning an irreverent reference to the old man and then hastily correcting himself to the respectful “Master.”
findings.rationale: The cut-off 노 initiates an informal or disrespectful reference to Jeok Cheongang; the immediate correction is a characterization and register joke.

findings.defect: The draft omits the comic self-correction from “a little” to “a lot.”
findings.rationale: 좀, 많이 deliberately revises the degree mid-sentence, preserving Taekyung’s sheepish humor after his scheme is exposed.
findings.replacement: “Did I make it a little… too obvious?”

findings.current: [^1]: The Southern Man was a historical term for the southern regions beyond the traditional Chinese heartland.
findings.defect: The note incorrectly presents “Southern Man” as a singular historical term and describes a people-oriented exonym merely as a label for regions.
findings.rationale: 南蠻 is a collective historical exonym associated with southern peoples and their territories; transliteration avoids the misleading singular phrase “the Southern Man.”
findings.replacement: [^1]: Nanman is a historical Chinese term—often translated as “Southern Barbarians”—for peoples and territories south of the traditional Chinese heartland.

findings.current: - A Sudden Quest, **Three-Strike Kill**, has been generated!
findings.defect: The quest title changes 招 from “move” to “strike,” even though the challenge is explicitly to withstand three moves.
findings.rationale: 三招殺 literally names a kill within three moves, matching the immediately stated condition that Taekyung endure Nangong Cheon’s 삼 초.
findings.replacement: - A Sudden Quest, **Three-Move Kill**, has been generated!

summary: Several actionable fidelity and terminology issues, chiefly altered subjects, a lost self-correction joke, and an incorrect rendering of 南蠻.
